      "body": "REPLACING A HAND-ROLLED HYPOTHESIS BY 'THE STANDARD ONE' CAN STRENGTHEN IT INTO FALSITY -- and the test is a REFUTATION probe at the intended object, not a satisfiability witness.\n\nMEASURED (pic-e, AJC 0095 r7). I built the vocabulary the project was missing (graded prime avoidance => FiniteInAffine for projective schemes, all sorry-free), then restated the seam's antecedent with IsProjective of the representing scheme in place of the elementary FiniteInAffine, and committed 'entirely in standard vocabulary, no condition invented in this project'. I ran THREE vacuity checks and all three PASSED: the new conjunct is satisfiable (Spec k is projective over itself), it is NOT free (exact? fails at an arbitrary object), and the new antecedent does not close hypothesis-free. A fresh-context audit then refuted it in one step.\n\nWHY THE CHECKS MISSED IT. Every one of them asks 'could this hypothesis hold SOMEWHERE?'. None asks 'does it hold AT THE OBJECT THE STATEMENT IS ABOUT?'. IsProjective over a field forces IsProper, hence UniversallyClosed, hence CompactSpace over the compact Spec k -- and Pic_{C/k} is a disjoint union over deg in Z, so it is not quasi-compact. The antecedent is FALSE at its only intended witness. Satisfiability elsewhere is exactly what makes that invisible.\n\nWORSE: my own project already had the refutation. Picard/AmbientPicNotProper.lean exists to record this as 'trap (c): a P -> Q whose antecedent is unsatisfiable in the intended setting', with the general theorems to check it -- and I had imported nothing from it. The strengthening was FROM a weak condition my own file proved holds at the curve TO one my own project proved fails at the Picard scheme.\n\nTHE GENERALISABLE RULE. When you replace a hypothesis H by a 'more standard' H', H' => H is not enough -- that direction is what makes the substitution LOOK conservative. Ask what H' implies that H does not (here: quasi-compactness), then check that consequence at the intended witness. My first repair -- 'every finite set that lies in a good open lies in an affine open' -- is PROVABLE for every scheme with its hypothesis unused.       "body": "AN 'ONLY PRODUCER IS FIELD-ONLY' CLAIM IS A CENSUS OF THE NAME YOU GUESSED, AND THE RING-LEVEL VERSION IS OFTEN LANDED UNDER A DIFFERENT MAP.\n\nMEASURED (pic-g 0096 r6, refuted by a fresh-context audit of my own file). I published that the picEtAffineEquiv/unit presentation seam has exactly one general producer -- PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section -- that it is stated over a FIELD and needs a curve section there, and that ring-level surjectivity of PicEtAff.unit is therefore the honest next brick. Every clause was checkable and the conclusion was false: picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt (PicEtUnit.lean:161) supplies the same seam at an ARBITRARY test RING, no field, no section, no curve binder, with 11 call sites.\n\nWHY MY CENSUS MISSED IT, and this is the reusable part. I searched for producers of the SEAM'S NAME -- surjectivity of  -- because that is the shape of the conclusion I wanted. The landed producer is not about 's surjectivity at all: it is an AFFINE-CONSISTENCY lemma for a DIFFERENT map (relPicToPicEt) which happens to have the seam as its conclusion. A grep for 'unit_surjective' finds it never; a search for the CONCLUSION 'picEtAffineEquiv _ = PicEtAff.unit _ _' finds it first.\n\nSO THE RULE: when you are about to write 'the only producer is X, and X is too strong', search for the CONCLUSION you need, not for the strengthened statement whose name you have. The name census answers 'who proved this lemma'; the obligation is 'who lands this Prop', and a lemma about another map can land it while carrying none of the binders you were about to price.\n\nAND THE SECOND-ORDER COST, which is why this is worth a memory item rather than a header note: the false claim RELOCATED THE GAP. I named ring-level surjectivity of  as the next brick; the actually-open statement is surjectivity of relPicToPicEt onto picEt -- a different map, different proof, and one the tree already treats as a real condition (Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:199 calls membership in its range 'honesty'). A misidentified next brick sends the next lane to build something nobody needs.",

      "body": "A \"TRAP, MEASURED -- DO NOT ROUTE VIA X\" NOTE IS THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE FALSE CLAIM A LANE CAN SHIP, AND THE CHEAPEST TEST IS TO GREP WHETHER A SIBLING FILE ALREADY DOES X.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (AJCR, pic-c 0092 r5, Pic0VanishingFieldGenusZero.lean:33-38). A lane recorded, in a file header, a commit message, and a direct message to another lane: \"going through chi_moduleKSheaf at baseChangeBundle C K produces the same object under a different Over instance, and the two chi terms DO NOT UNIFY -- measured\". It reads like exactly the kind of hard-won spelling fact worth broadcasting, and the receiving lane accepted it.\n\nIt is false. The bundled route closes with one `change` to the bundled spelling followed by `simpa`, at DEFAULT heartbeats. What had been measured was that one `simpa` failed without the `change`, i.e. a fact about a tactic invocation, published as a fact about two objects.\n\nTHE TEST THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT COST ONE GREP. A sibling lane had written the prohibited proof, at a concrete curve, in the same hour, and it was at HEAD and root-imported: Curve/P1DegreeZeroTrivial.lean:83-99 uses chi_moduleKSheaf at baseChangeBundle with the same change + simpa. So before publishing \"route X does not work\", grep the tree for X: a live use site refutes the prohibition outright, and its presence in a file you did not write is more likely than it feels, because a prohibition is usually discovered exactly when two lanes are on the same object.\n\nWHY IT IS WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY OVERCLAIM. A positive overclaim gets tested when someone tries to use the result. A prohibition is never tested -- its whole function is to stop people trying -- so it can survive indefinitely and it forecloses a cheap route for every later round. Same asymmetry as [[gap-list-is-the-least-audited-prose]] and [[exculpatory-sentence-is-a-claim]], but with a longer half-life.\n\nCOROLLARY, same round, same file: unexplained `set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000` raises with a comment asserting the default is exceeded. Copying both files verbatim with the default budget: EXIT=0, all six declarations. A budget raise is a claim too, and re-running the file at the default is a 40-second check.",

      "body": "A LOCALISATION REDUCTION IS EMPTIED BY THE CONSUMER OWN OUTER QUANTIFIER, AND EVERY PER-STATEMENT CHECK PASSES.\n\nMEASURED (pic-g, AJCR 0096 r7, Pic0RingZariskiLocal.lean; audit I-1657/I-1660, reproduced by me).\n\nWHAT HAPPENED. I reduced an obligation P(A) at an arbitrary test algebra to a pointwise-local form: for every prime p of A, some f outside p with P(Localization.Away f). At a FIXED A that is a real reduction with no route back, and I verified it. I then composed it over all A into two producers of the goal object -- and those hypotheses are LOGICALLY EQUIVALENT to the global ones they were meant to weaken, because Localization.Away f is ITSELF a test algebra, so the consumer own forall-A already ranges over it. The converse is one line with the trivial witness f = 1.\n\nWHY EVERY CHECK PASSED. Sorry-free, axiom-clean against a sorryAx control, rooted, build green, non-vacuous (both hypotheses used, linter clean), and the fixed-A lemma genuinely is a reduction. Nothing local to any statement is wrong. The defect is the INTERACTION between my inner quantifier and the consumer outer one, and no per-statement check can see it.\n\nTHE TEST, and it costs one probe: before pricing a localisation, pointwise, or restriction reduction as progress, PROVE THE CONVERSE WITH THE TRIVIAL WITNESS -- f = 1, the identity localisation, V = top, the whole space. If it closes, the reduction only helps at a FIXED base object, and you must then check whether the consumer has that shape. Mine did not.\n\nSECOND, SMALLER TRAP FROM THE SAME FILE: my \"local ring\" interface was about Localization.Away f, which is a BASIC OPEN and not a local ring (IsLocalRing fails to synthesize). A lane with a genuinely local computation holds Localization.AtPrime, and the AtPrime-to-Away bridge is spreading out -- ask which one your consumer actually has before naming the interface.\n\nSibling of \"substitute the trivial value in layer one\" and \"free factor vs localisation\".",

      "body": "A --summary WRITE IS A SILENT DESTRUCTIVE EDIT, AND THE TOOL'S OWN OUTPUT CANNOT SHOW IT. Check the commit STAT, not the command's success line.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (pic-c, AJCR 0092 r1). I claimed a row with roadmap set --owner --status --summary. The CLI printed 'Updated roadmap item' and nothing else. The commit stat then read 46 insertions / 117 DELETIONS. --summary REPLACES; the 117 lines were review-ajcr's rank-elevation analysis of that exact fork, TWO author self-retractions inside it, and the row's stated live target. I had read the row earlier in the session, but through roadmap list, which truncates -- so I never saw the body I was about to overwrite.\n\nWHY THE EXISTING LESSONS DO NOT COVER IT. The workspace has roadmap-yaml-edit-reverts-owner (a prose edit writing a stale OWNER over a live claim) and several items about staged deletions of other lanes' FILES. This is neither: the owner field was fine, no file was staged D, the write was to a row I legitimately hold, and the loss was entirely inside one YAML string. Every file-level check passes.\n\nTHE RULE, cheap and it is the only one that works. After any roadmap set --summary, read the commit stat. A deletion count above a handful means you replaced prose you never read. Recover with git show <commit>^:<path>, merge the prior summary verbatim, append yours behind a marker saying what happened, and re-verify a distinctive phrase from the old text is present.\n\nTHE SHARPER POINT. The destroyed text contained a retraction whose lesson was 'a probe with the hypothesis as a BINDER measures the conversion, so the control looks audited' -- i.e. I deleted a warning about exactly the class of error a reviewer had just caught me making elsewhere in the same session. Board prose is where a lane's corrections live, and it is the least protected thing in the workspace: no build breaks, no test fails, no file appears deleted.",

          "body": "RIDER, and it nearly caused a second bogus repair. Verify board prose by PARSING the summary field, never by grepping the file.\n\nAfter a roadmap set --pin-commit write I grepped for my newly appended section and got 0 hits, concluded the CLI had clobbered me again, and started re-appending. The grep was wrong, not the CLI: yaml.safe_dump wraps at 88 columns, so any phrase longer than a few words spans lines and no grep can match it. python3 -c \"yaml.safe_load(...)[\\\"summary\\\"]\" then showed all five distinctive phrases present, 14685 chars, three pins, owner cleared.\n\nSo the original rule (check the commit STAT) stands, and this is its companion: a zero grep hit on board prose is evidence about line wrapping, not about content. Both halves matter -- the stat catches real loss, and parsing prevents inventing loss that did not happen."

      "body": "A THREE-LANE COMPOSITION IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY PER-ROW CHECK, AND THE ROWS WILL EACH TELL YOU THE WORK IS ELSEWHERE.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (pic-e, AJC, 0095 r6). Three sorry-free theorems from three different lanes composed into a verbatim derivation of the project's central sorry from the classical pointed theorem: the unconditional finite-GALOIS-level rational point (Curve/), the picSharp->picEt transport (PicEtSubcanonical), and the lftFree descent step with hq and hcov already internal (PicEtGaloisQuotient). Eleven declarations, all axiom-clean, three commits.\n\nNO ROW MENTIONED THE OTHER TWO. The descent-assembly row listed FOUR open inputs; three were already discharged elsewhere. The seam docstring's own 'what remains' sentence listed three items, one of which was closed and one of which was DONE-AND-CALLED-REMAINING. Every row was individually plausible and internally consistent; the composition existed only across them.\n\nTHE MECHANISM, and why the usual checks miss it: each row is maintained by the lane that owns it, and a lane records what IT owes, not what another lane has since supplied. So a row goes stale in the CHEAP direction -- it schedules work that exists -- and nothing re-reads it, because a list of remaining obligations reads as self-criticism. Same asymmetry as [[gap-list-is-the-least-audited-prose]] and [[unavoidable-is-not-geometric]], but distributed: no single sentence is wrong enough to notice.\n\nTHE CHECK THAT FINDS IT, and it is cheap: take the consumer theorem's LITERAL binder list -- #check the one a costing tells you to aim at -- and ask of EACH binder, separately, 'does a producer for exactly this exist at HEAD?'. Not 'is this gap open' (the row answers that) but 'is this BINDER discharged'. At the spelling that matters, seamClauseOne_of_hasGaloisQuotient_lftFree, three of four were gone and the fourth was an instance binder no row named. A four-item gap list and a one-item binder list were both accurate about different things.\n\nCOROLLARY, the part that cost me a withdrawal: after composing, price the RESULT against the WEAKEST antecedent your proof consumes, not the shape the hand-off wants. My first antecedent carried IsSeparated, which is provably free from the conclusion's own representation, and a reduction whose antecedent contains a free conjunct misreports exactly the number it exists to report. Related: [[price-the-consumer-carrier]], [[audit-the-goals-antecedents-not-the-lemmas]].",

      "body": "VANISHING-VOCABULARY SPELLINGS ARE ONE ANTECEDENT -- and the commit that ships the 'reduced' producer often ships the iff that proves it is a re-spelling.\n\nAJC DivFamilyZero.lean, AJC.picrep.divzero, pic-e runs 0095->0105. Over three rounds the same lane landed three producers of Div0-representable, each 'reducing' the obligation to a fresh vocabulary:\n  _of_isZero               : IsZero x.F\n  _of_forall_subsingleton_sections : forall V, Subsingleton Gamma(x.F,V)\n  _of_forall_isEmpty_schematicSupport : IsEmpty(schematicSupport x.F)\nEach docstring bills its antecedent as 'the sharpest/purest/most-geometric honest form.' At every DivFamily x.F is quasicoherent, and the file itself ships isZero_iff_forall_subsingleton_sections and isZero_iff_isEmpty_schematicSupport -- so the three antecedents are PROVABLY EQUIVALENT (all = IsZero x.F). None is weaker. The obligation HasFiberDeg 0 -> IsZero x.F is untouched; only the vocabulary on its RHS rotates.\n\nTHE TELL, sharper than I-1622: when a 'reduction' commit also lands an IFF between the new antecedent and the old one, the iff IS the proof that no reduction happened. Emptiness-of-support, subsingleton-sections, and IsZero are one node with three names; a producer parameterised on any of them is the same producer. Before crediting 'reduced to X', rw the shipped iffs and check whether the new antecedent closes the old goal with no hypotheses -- if it does, it is coordinates, not distance. The real distance for divzero lives in DivSupportQuasiFinite.lean (carrier bridge + degree-0=>empty-fibre), which no spelling of the RHS moves.",

/-!
# The category of sheaves of modules over a scheme

In this file, we define the abelian category of sheaves of modules
`X.Modules` over a scheme `X`, and study its basic functoriality.

-/

@[expose] public section

universe t u

open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace SheafOfModules Bicategory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

variable {X Y Z T : Scheme.{u}}

variable (X) in
/-- The category of sheaves of modules over a scheme. -/
def Modules := SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf

namespace Modules

/-- Morphisms between `𝒪ₓ`-modules. Use `Hom.app` to act on sections. -/
def Hom (M N : X.Modules) : Type u := SheafOfModules.Hom M N

instance : Category X.Modules where
  Hom := Modules.Hom
  __ := (inferInstance : Category (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf))

noncomputable instance : Abelian X.Modules :=
  inferInstanceAs <| Abelian (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf)
instance : HasLimits X.Modules := inferInstanceAs (HasLimits (SheafOfModules X.ringCatSheaf))
instance : HasColimits X.Modules := inferInstanceAs (HasColimits (SheafOfModules X.ringCatSheaf))

section Functor

variable (X) in
/-- The forgetful functor from `𝒪ₓ`-modules to presheaves of modules.
This is mostly useful to transport results from (pre)sheaves of modules to `𝒪ₓ`-modules and
usually shouldn't be used directly when working with actual `𝒪ₓ`-modules. -/
def toPresheafOfModules : X.Modules ⥤ X.PresheafOfModules := SheafOfModules.forget _

/-- The forgetful functor from `𝒪ₓ`-modules to presheaves of modules is fully faithful. -/
def fullyFaithfulToPresheafOfModules : (Modules.toPresheafOfModules X).FullyFaithful :=
  SheafOfModules.fullyFaithfulForget _

instance : (toPresheafOfModules X).Full := fullyFaithfulToPresheafOfModules.full
instance : (toPresheafOfModules X).Faithful := fullyFaithfulToPresheafOfModules.faithful
instance : (toPresheafOfModules X).IsRightAdjoint :=
  (PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).isRightAdjoint

variable (X) in
/-- The forgetful functor from `𝒪ₓ`-modules to presheaves of abelian groups. -/
noncomputable def toPresheaf : X.Modules ⥤ TopCat.Presheaf Ab X :=
  toPresheafOfModules X ⋙ PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf _

instance : (toPresheaf X).Faithful := .comp _ (PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf _)
instance : PreservesLimits (toPresheaf X) := comp_preservesLimits _ (PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf _)
instance : (toPresheaf X).ReflectsIsomorphisms :=
  reflectsIsomorphisms_comp _ (PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf _)

end Functor

variable {M N K : X.Modules} {φ : M ⟶ N} {U V : X.Opens}

section Presheaf

/-- The underlying abelian presheaf of an `𝒪ₓ`-module. -/
noncomputable def presheaf (M : X.Modules) : TopCat.Presheaf Ab X := M.1.presheaf

/-- Notation for sections of a presheaf of module. -/
scoped[AlgebraicGeometry] notation3 "Γ(" M ", " U ")" => (Scheme.Modules.presheaf M).obj (.op U)

instance : Module Γ(X, U) Γ(M, U) := (M.val.obj (.op U)).isModule

variable (M) in
@[simp] lemma map_smul (i : U ⟶ V) (r : Γ(X, V)) (x : Γ(M, V)) :
    M.presheaf.map i.op (r • x) = X.presheaf.map i.op r • M.presheaf.map i.op x :=
  M.val.map_smul _ _ _

/-- Scalar multiplication as an endomorphism of `Γ(M, U)`. -/
def smul : Γ(X, U) →+* End Γ(M, U) :=
  (M.val.obj (.op U)).smul

@[simp]
lemma smul_apply (r : Γ(X, U)) (x : Γ(M, U)) : (M.smul r).hom x = r • x := rfl

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma map_comp_smul (i : U ⟶ V) (r : Γ(X, V)) :
    M.smul r ≫ M.presheaf.map i.op = M.presheaf.map i.op ≫ M.smul (X.presheaf.map i.op r) := by
  ext
  simp

/-- The underlying map between abelian presheaves of a morphism of `𝒪ₓ`-modules. -/
noncomputable def Hom.mapPresheaf (φ : M ⟶ N) : M.presheaf ⟶ N.presheaf :=
  (toPresheaf X).map φ

/-- The application of a morphism of `𝒪ₓ`-modules to sections. -/
def Hom.app (φ : M ⟶ N) (U : X.Opens) : Γ(M, U) ⟶ Γ(N, U) :=
  (forget₂ _ _).map (φ.val.app (.op U))

@[simp] lemma mapPresheaf_app (φ : M ⟶ N) (U) : φ.mapPresheaf.app U = φ.app U.unop := rfl

@[simp]
lemma Hom.app_smul (φ : M ⟶ N) (r : Γ(X, U)) (x : Γ(M, U)) :
    φ.app U (r • x) = r • φ.app U x :=
  (φ.val.app (.op U)).hom.map_smul r x

@[simp] lemma Hom.add_app (φ ψ : M ⟶ N) : (φ + ψ).app U = φ.app U + ψ.app U := rfl
@[simp] lemma Hom.sub_app (φ ψ : M ⟶ N) : (φ - ψ).app U = φ.app U - ψ.app U := rfl
@[simp] lemma Hom.zero_app : (0 : M ⟶ N).app U = 0 := rfl
@[simp] lemma Hom.id_app (M : X.Modules) : (𝟙 M :).app U = 𝟙 _ := rfl
@[simp] lemma Hom.comp_app (φ : M ⟶ N) (ψ : N ⟶ K) : (φ ≫ ψ).app U = φ.app U ≫ ψ.app U := rfl

@[ext]
lemma hom_ext (f g : M ⟶ N) (H : ∀ U, f.app U = g.app U) : f = g := by
  apply SheafOfModules.hom_ext
  ext U x
  exact congr($(H U.unop) x)

lemma isSheaf (M : X.Modules) : M.presheaf.IsSheaf := SheafOfModules.isSheaf M

@[simp] lemma toPresheaf_obj : (toPresheaf X).obj M = M.presheaf := rfl
@[simp] lemma toPresheaf_map : (toPresheaf X).map φ = φ.mapPresheaf := rfl

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
lemma Hom.isIso_iff_isIso_app {M N : X.Modules} {φ : M ⟶ N} :
    IsIso φ ↔ ∀ U, IsIso (φ.app U) := by
  rw [← isIso_iff_of_reflects_iso _ (toPresheaf X), NatTrans.isIso_iff_isIso_app]
  simp [Opposite.op_surjective.forall]

instance [IsIso φ] : IsIso (φ.app U) := Hom.isIso_iff_isIso_app.mp ‹_› _

@[simp, push ←]
lemma inv_app [IsIso φ] : (inv φ).app U = inv (φ.app U) := by
  apply IsIso.eq_inv_of_hom_inv_id
  simp [← Hom.comp_app]

end Presheaf

noncomputable section Functorial

variable (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (h : Z ⟶ T)

/-- The pushforward functor for categories of sheaves of modules over schemes. -/
def pushforward : X.Modules ⥤ Y.Modules :=
  SheafOfModules.pushforward f.toRingCatSheafHom

@[simp]
lemma pushforward_obj_obj (M : X.Modules) (U : Y.Opens) :
    Γ((pushforward f).obj M, U) = Γ(M, f ⁻¹ᵁ U) := rfl

@[simp]
lemma pushforward_obj_presheaf_map {U V : Y.Opens} (i : U ⟶ V) :
    ((pushforward f).obj M).presheaf.map i.op = M.presheaf.map ((Opens.map f.base).map i).op := rfl

@[simp]
lemma pushforward_map_app (φ : M ⟶ N) (U : Y.Opens) :
    ((pushforward f).map φ).app U = φ.app (f ⁻¹ᵁ U) := rfl

/-- The pullback functor for categories of sheaves of modules over schemes. -/
def pullback : Y.Modules ⥤ X.Modules :=
  SheafOfModules.pullback f.toRingCatSheafHom

/-- The pullback functor for categories of sheaves of modules over schemes
is left adjoint to the pushforward functor. -/
def pullbackPushforwardAdjunction : pullback f ⊣ pushforward f :=
  SheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction _

section

attribute [local instance] preservesBinaryBiproducts_of_preservesBinaryCoproducts
  preservesBinaryBiproducts_of_preservesBinaryProducts

instance : (pullback f).IsLeftAdjoint := (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f).isLeftAdjoint
instance : (pushforward f).IsRightAdjoint := (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f).isRightAdjoint
instance : (pushforward f).Additive := Functor.additive_of_preservesBinaryBiproducts _
instance : (pullback f).Additive := Functor.additive_of_preservesBinaryBiproducts _

end

variable (X) in
/-- The pushforward of sheaves of modules by the identity morphism identifies
to the identity functor. -/
def pushforwardId : pushforward (𝟙 X) ≅ 𝟭 _ :=
  SheafOfModules.pushforwardId _

@[simp] lemma pushforwardId_hom_app_app : ((pushforwardId X).hom.app M).app U = 𝟙 _ := rfl
@[simp] lemma pushforwardId_inv_app_app : ((pushforwardId X).inv.app M).app U = 𝟙 _ := rfl

variable (X) in
/-- The pullback of sheaves of modules by the identity morphism identifies
to the identity functor. -/
def pullbackId : pullback (𝟙 X) ≅ 𝟭 _ :=
  SheafOfModules.pullbackId _

variable (X) in
lemma conjugateEquiv_pullbackId_hom :
    conjugateEquiv .id (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (𝟙 X)) (pullbackId X).hom =
      (pushforwardId X).inv :=
  SheafOfModules.conjugateEquiv_pullbackId_hom _

/-- The composition of two pushforward functors for sheaves of modules on schemes
identify to the pushforward for the composition. -/
def pushforwardComp :
    pushforward f ⋙ pushforward g ≅ pushforward (f ≫ g) :=
  SheafOfModules.pushforwardComp _ _

@[simp] lemma pushforwardComp_hom_app_app (U) : ((pushforwardComp f g).hom.app M).app U = 𝟙 _ := rfl
@[simp] lemma pushforwardComp_inv_app_app (U) : ((pushforwardComp f g).inv.app M).app U = 𝟙 _ := rfl

/-!
# Restricting a scheme module to the base ring

For a scheme `X` over `Spec k`, this file views an `X.Modules` object as a sheaf of
`k`-modules.  The construction keeps the same section types and restriction maps; only the
scalar action is restricted along `k -> Gamma(X, U)`.  It is the dialect bridge needed to
compare a `Scheme.Modules` line bundle with the fixed-base module sheaves used by the Cech
cohomology engine.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

variable {k : Type u} [CommRing k]

/-- The base-ring module structure on sections of a scheme module. -/
@[reducible] noncomputable def moduleKSections
    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : X.left.Modules)
    (U : X.left.Opens) : Module k Γ(M, U) :=
  Module.compHom _ (X.left.overAlgebraMap k U)

attribute [local instance] moduleKSections

/-- The native structure-sheaf action, with section-notation binders kept explicit. -/
private noncomputable def smulSection
    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : X.left.Modules)
    (U : X.left.Opens) (r : Γ(X.left, U)) (x : Γ(M, U)) : Γ(M, U) :=
  r • x

/-- The presheaf underlying a scheme module after restriction of scalars to the base ring. -/
noncomputable def toModuleKPresheafOfModules
    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : X.left.Modules) :
    X.left.Opensᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} k where
  obj U := ModuleCat.of k Γ(M, U.unop)
  map {U V} f := ModuleCat.ofHom
    { toFun := fun x => M.presheaf.map f x
      map_add' := fun x y => map_add _ x y
      map_smul' := fun r x =>
        (Scheme.Modules.map_smul M f.unop (X.left.overAlgebraMap k U.unop r) x).trans
          (congrArg
            (fun (s : Γ(X.left, V.unop)) =>
              smulSection X M V.unop s (M.presheaf.map f x))
            (X.left.overAlgebraMap_apply_res k f r)) }
  map_id U := by
    ext x
    exact congrFun (congrArg (fun (f : M.presheaf.obj U ⟶ M.presheaf.obj U) =>
      (ConcreteCategory.hom f : _ → _)) (M.presheaf.map_id U)) x
  map_comp {U V W} f g := by
    ext x
    exact congrFun (congrArg (fun (h : M.presheaf.obj U ⟶ M.presheaf.obj W) =>
      (ConcreteCategory.hom h : _ → _)) (M.presheaf.map_comp f g)) x

/-- The restricted presheaf is a sheaf because its underlying additive presheaf is unchanged. -/
lemma toModuleKPresheafOfModules_isSheaf
    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : X.left.Modules) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.left.toTopCat)
      (toModuleKPresheafOfModules X M) := by
  rw [Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget _ _ (CategoryTheory.forget (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
  convert (Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget _ _
      (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u})).mp (Scheme.Modules.isSheaf M) using 1 <;> rfl

/-- A sheaf of `O_X`-modules, viewed as a sheaf of modules over the base ring. -/
noncomputable def toModuleKSheafOfModules
    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : X.left.Modules) :
    Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k) :=
  ⟨toModuleKPresheafOfModules X M, toModuleKPresheafOfModules_isSheaf X M⟩

/-- Restriction maps of the base-ring sheaf are definitionally those of the scheme module. -/
lemma toModuleKSheafOfModules_obj_map_apply
    {X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (M : X.left.Modules)
    {V W : X.left.Opens} (h : W ≤ V)
    (x : (toModuleKSheafOfModules X M).obj.obj (op V)) :
    ((toModuleKSheafOfModules X M).obj.map (homOfLE h).op).hom x =
      M.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op x :=
  rfl

namespace Modules

variable {X : Scheme.{u}}

/-- A scheme module which is locally isomorphic to the structure sheaf. -/
def IsLineBundle (M : X.Modules) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧
    Nonempty ((restrictFunctor U.ι).obj M ≅ SheafOfModules.unit U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf)

end Modules

end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

/-- **Quasi-coherence packaging** of a sheaf `F` of `k`-modules on an open `U` of a
scheme `X`: an action of the fixed section ring `Γ(X, U)` on the `F`-sections over each
open `W ≤ U`, natural under restriction (the (P1) mixin), together with localization of
`F`-sections away from `g ∈ Γ(X, U)` on affine opens `V ≤ U`, in the two-lemma form of
`IsLocalization.Away` (the (P2) axioms). This is exactly the data consumed by Serre's
affine degree-one vanishing argument
(`IsAffineOpen.subsingleton_hModule'_one_of_qcoh`,
`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.AffineVanishingQcoh`).

The structure sheaf satisfies the packaging on every open
(`Scheme.moduleKSheaf.instQcohOn`); sheaves trivialized on an affine chart `U` (the
Wave-4 twisted line bundles) satisfy it chart by chart. -/
class Scheme.QcohOn (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology (X : TopCat)) (ModuleCat.{u} k))
    (U : X.Opens) where
  /-- The action of an ambient section `r ∈ Γ(X, U)` on `F`-sections over `W ≤ U`. -/
  qsmul {W : X.Opens} (hWU : W ≤ U) : Γ(X, U) → F.obj.obj (op W) → F.obj.obj (op W)
  /-- The action of `1`. -/
  one_qsmul {W : X.Opens} (hWU : W ≤ U) (m : F.obj.obj (op W)) : qsmul hWU 1 m = m
  /-- The action of a product. -/
  mul_qsmul {W : X.Opens} (hWU : W ≤ U) (r s : Γ(X, U)) (m : F.obj.obj (op W)) :
    qsmul hWU (r * s) m = qsmul hWU r (qsmul hWU s m)
  /-- The action distributes over addition of scalars. -/
  add_qsmul {W : X.Opens} (hWU : W ≤ U) (r s : Γ(X, U)) (m : F.obj.obj (op W)) :
    qsmul hWU (r + s) m = qsmul hWU r m + qsmul hWU s m
  /-- The action distributes over addition of sections. -/
  qsmul_add {W : X.Opens} (hWU : W ≤ U) (r : Γ(X, U)) (m n : F.obj.obj (op W)) :
    qsmul hWU r (m + n) = qsmul hWU r m + qsmul hWU r n
  /-- The action is natural under restriction of `F`-sections. -/
  secRes_qsmul {V W : X.Opens} (hVW : V ≤ W) (hWU : W ≤ U) (r : Γ(X, U))
      (m : F.obj.obj (op W)) :
    secRes F hVW (qsmul hWU r m) = qsmul (hVW.trans hWU) r (secRes F hVW m)
  /-- **(P2) denominator clearing** on affine opens of `U`: a section of `F` over
  `V ⊓ D(g)` becomes the restriction of a section over `V` after scaling by a power
  of `g`. -/
  exists_secRes_eq_qsmul_pow {V : X.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (hVU : V ≤ U)
      (g : Γ(X, U)) (c : F.obj.obj (op (V ⊓ X.basicOpen g))) :
      ∃ (N : ℕ) (e : F.obj.obj (op V)),
        secRes F inf_le_left e =
          qsmul ((inf_le_left : V ⊓ X.basicOpen g ≤ V).trans hVU) (g ^ N) c
  /-- **(P2) defect annihilation** on affine opens of `U`: a section of `F` over `V`
  restricting to zero on `V ⊓ D(g)` is killed by a power of `g`. -/
  exists_qsmul_pow_eq_zero {V : X.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (hVU : V ≤ U)
      (g : Γ(X, U)) (t : F.obj.obj (op V))
      (ht : secRes F (inf_le_left : V ⊓ X.basicOpen g ≤ V) t = 0) :
      ∃ M : ℕ, qsmul hVU (g ^ M) t = 0

namespace Scheme.QcohOn

variable {F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology (X : TopCat)) (ModuleCat.{u} k)}
  {U : X.Opens} [Scheme.QcohOn F U] {W : X.Opens}

/-- The inclusion-proof argument of the action is proof-irrelevant. -/
lemma qsmul_proof_irrel (h₁ h₂ : W ≤ U) (r : Γ(X, U)) (m : F.obj.obj (op W)) :
    qsmul h₁ r m = qsmul h₂ r m := rfl

/-- The action of a scalar on the zero section. -/
lemma qsmul_zero (hWU : W ≤ U) (r : Γ(X, U)) :
    qsmul hWU r (0 : F.obj.obj (op W)) = 0 := by
  have h := qsmul_add hWU r (0 : F.obj.obj (op W)) 0
  rw [add_zero] at h
  have h2 : qsmul hWU r (0 : F.obj.obj (op W)) + 0 =
      qsmul hWU r (0 : F.obj.obj (op W)) + qsmul hWU r 0 := by
    rw [add_zero]
    exact h
  exact (add_left_cancel h2).symm

/-- The action distributes over subtraction of sections. -/
lemma qsmul_sub (hWU : W ≤ U) (r : Γ(X, U)) (m n : F.obj.obj (op W)) :
    qsmul hWU r (m - n) = qsmul hWU r m - qsmul hWU r n := by
  rw [eq_sub_iff_add_eq, ← qsmul_add, sub_add_cancel]

/-- The action of a finite sum of scalars. -/
lemma sum_qsmul {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (hWU : W ≤ U) (c : ι → Γ(X, U))
    (m : F.obj.obj (op W)) :
    qsmul hWU (∑ i ∈ s, c i) m = ∑ i ∈ s, qsmul hWU (c i) m :=
  map_sum (AddMonoidHom.mk' (fun r ↦ qsmul hWU r m) fun r r' ↦ add_qsmul hWU r r' m) c s

end Scheme.QcohOn

section StructureSheaf

/-! ### The structure sheaf satisfies the packaging

`Scheme.moduleKSheaf k` carries the tautological action `qsmul h r s = X.resHom h r * s`
of ambient sections, natural under restriction since restriction is a ring homomorphism;
the localization axioms are the landed affine-open localization lemmas of
`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.AffineCech`. This instance recovers the landed
structure-sheaf vanishing (`IsAffineOpen.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one`) as a
special case of the generalized engine. -/

variable [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]

/-- Reinterpret a section of `X.moduleKSheaf k` over `W` as a scheme section in
`Γ(X, W)`. The two types are definitionally equal; this identity bridge pins the
`Γ`-spelling so that ring operations elaborate without coercion noise. -/
private def moduleKSheafToΓ {W : X.Opens} (s : (X.moduleKSheaf k).obj.obj (op W)) :
    Γ(X, W) := s

/-- The structure sheaf as a sheaf of `k`-modules is quasi-coherently packaged on every
open `U`: ambient sections act by restriction-then-multiplication, and the localization
axioms are `IsAffineOpen.exists_res_eq_pow_mul` and
`IsAffineOpen.exists_pow_mul_eq_zero_of_res_eq_zero`. -/
noncomputable instance Scheme.moduleKSheaf.instQcohOn (U : X.Opens) :
    Scheme.QcohOn (X.moduleKSheaf k) U where
  qsmul {W} hWU r s := X.resHom hWU r * moduleKSheafToΓ s
  one_qsmul {W} hWU m := by
    change X.resHom hWU 1 * moduleKSheafToΓ m = moduleKSheafToΓ m
    rw [map_one, one_mul]
  mul_qsmul {W} hWU r s m := by
    change X.resHom hWU (r * s) * moduleKSheafToΓ m =
      X.resHom hWU r * (X.resHom hWU s * moduleKSheafToΓ m)
    rw [map_mul, mul_assoc]
  add_qsmul {W} hWU r s m := by
    change X.resHom hWU (r + s) * moduleKSheafToΓ m =
      X.resHom hWU r * moduleKSheafToΓ m + X.resHom hWU s * moduleKSheafToΓ m
    rw [map_add, add_mul]
    rw [Scheme.resHom_resHom]
    exact hz2
  choose M₁ hM₁ using hann
  refine ⟨Finset.univ.sup M₁, ?_⟩
  refine gluedSubmodule_ext k U g σ (fun i => X.basicOpen (h i)) hP
    (hV'V.trans hcov) fun i => ?_
  have hz : (0 : ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g V')).val (σ i) = 0 := rfl
  rw [gluedQsmul_coe, hz, map_zero, map_mul, map_pow, map_pow]
  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom]
  rw [← Nat.sub_add_cancel (Finset.le_sup (Finset.mem_univ i) :
      M₁ i ≤ Finset.univ.sup M₁),
    pow_add, mul_assoc, hM₁ i, mul_zero]

/-- **The quasi-coherence packaging of the glued sheaf** on a chart carrying a finite
trivializing subordinate basic-open family (DAT-1 stage 1b): the componentwise (P1)
action together with the two (P2) localization axioms. A `def`: keyed `instance`s are
declared only at the pinned datum (stage 1d), per the house instance discipline. -/
@[reducible] noncomputable def gluedQcohOn (hc : Scheme.IsGluingCocycle U g)
    (hP : ∀ i : ι, X.basicOpen (h i) ≤ U (σ i))
    (hcov : V ≤ ⨆ i : ι, X.basicOpen (h i)) :
    Scheme.QcohOn (gluedSheaf k U g) V where
  qsmul hWV r s := gluedQsmul k U g hWV r s
  one_qsmul hWV s := gluedQsmul_one k U g hWV s
  mul_qsmul hWV r r' s := gluedQsmul_mul k U g hWV r r' s
  add_qsmul hWV r r' s := gluedQsmul_add_left k U g hWV r r' s
  qsmul_add hWV r s t := gluedQsmul_add k U g hWV r s t
  secRes_qsmul hW'W hWV r s := gluedRes_gluedQsmul k U g hW'W hWV r s
  exists_secRes_eq_qsmul_pow hV' hV'V q c :=
    exists_gluedRes_eq_gluedQsmul_pow k U g hc hP hcov hV' hV'V q c
  exists_qsmul_pow_eq_zero hV' hV'V q t ht :=
    exists_gluedQsmul_pow_eq_zero k U g hP hcov hV' hV'V q t ht

end Assembly

/-!
# Invertible sections of a cocycle-glued line bundle on an affine open

The cocycle pieces used to construct `gluedSheaf` need not contain an arbitrary affine
open.  Nevertheless, every affine open admits a finite basic-open refinement subordinate
to the canonical pointed cover by those pieces.  On each refined basic open the glued
sheaf is free of rank one.  The existing localization-span engine then proves that its
sections on the original affine open are finite projective.

`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.AffineSectionsModel` packages the quasi-coherent action chosen by
that internal refinement together with the finite, projective, and invertible instances.
Returning a `Nonempty` model keeps the refinement choice noncomputable while giving
downstream code a single datum from which it can install all four compatible instances.

This is the chart-free line-bundle substrate needed to restrict a positive theta twist to
the arbitrary affine pieces of `AffAdaptation`: the divisor cover is not required to lie in
either pinned theta chart.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom pi]

namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum

/-- A compatible quasi-coherent module structure on the sections of a cocycle-glued
line bundle over an affine open, together with its finite projective rank-one properties.

The module instance is written explicitly in the fields so that it is definitionally the
one induced by `qcoh`; a consumer may install `M.qcoh` and recover `M.finite` and
`M.projective` without any proof-irrelevance transport. -/
structure AffineSectionsModel (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    (V : (relCurve C B).Opens) where
  qcoh : Scheme.QcohOn D.sheaf V
  qsmul_eq : ∀ {W : (relCurve C B).Opens} (hWV : W ≤ V) (r : Γ(relCurve C B, V))
      (s : D.sheaf.obj.obj (op W)),
      letI := qcoh
      Scheme.QcohOn.qsmul (F := D.sheaf) hWV r s =
        gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit hWV r s
  finite : @Module.Finite Γ(relCurve C B, V) (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V))
    _ _ (@Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE B _ (relCurve C B) V D.sheaf qcoh V (le_refl V))
  projective : @Module.Projective Γ(relCurve C B, V) _
    (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V)) _
    (@Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE B _ (relCurve C B) V D.sheaf qcoh V (le_refl V))
  invertible : @Module.Invertible Γ(relCurve C B, V) (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V))
    _ _ (@Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE B _ (relCurve C B) V D.sheaf qcoh V (le_refl V))

/-- Sections of a cocycle-glued line bundle on every affine open admit a compatible
invertible module model.  The proof chooses a finite basic-open refinement of the canonical
pointed cover, trivializes after the resulting faithfully flat product localization, and
descends invertibility; finiteness and projectivity are recorded on the same action. -/
theorem nonempty_affineSectionsModel (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    (V : (relCurve C B).Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V) :
    Nonempty (D.AffineSectionsModel V) := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨ι, fint, f, anchor, coeff, hP, hpart⟩ :=
    hV.exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement D.pointedCover
  letI : Fintype ι := fint
  let sigma : ι → D.index := fun i => D.pieceIndex (anchor i)
  have hP' : ∀ i : ι, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i) ≤ D.pieces (sigma i) := hP
  have hcov : V ≤ ⨆ i : ι, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i) :=
    le_iSup_basicOpen_of_sum_eq_one coeff f hpart
  let q : Scheme.QcohOn D.sheaf V :=
    gluedQcohOn B D.pieces D.unit D.isGluingCocycle hP' hcov
  letI : Scheme.QcohOn D.sheaf V := q
  let m : Module Γ(relCurve C B, V) (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V)) :=
    Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE (F := D.sheaf) (le_refl V)
  have hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤ :=
    Ideal.span_range_eq_top_of_sum_eq_one coeff f hpart
  have hfin : @Module.Finite Γ(relCurve C B, V) (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V)) _ _ m :=
    moduleFinite_glued B D.pieces D.unit hV D.isGluingCocycle
      (fun _ _ _ => rfl) hP' hspan
  have hproj : @Module.Projective Γ(relCurve C B, V) _
      (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V)) _ m :=
    projective_glued B D.pieces D.unit hV D.isGluingCocycle
      (fun _ _ _ => rfl) hP' hspan
  letI pieceBaseModule : ∀ i : ι, Module Γ(relCurve C B, V)
      (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op ((relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i)))) := fun i =>
    Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE (F := D.sheaf) ((relCurve C B).basicOpen_le (f i))
  letI pieceModule : ∀ i : ι,
      Module Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i))
        (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op ((relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i)))) := fun i =>
    gluedPieceModule B D.pieces D.unit D.isGluingCocycle hP' i
  letI pieceTower : ∀ i : ι, IsScalarTower Γ(relCurve C B, V)
      Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i))
      (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op ((relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i)))) := fun i =>
    isScalarTower_chart_piece B D.pieces D.unit D.isGluingCocycle
      (fun _ _ _ => rfl) hP' i
  letI pieceLocalization : ∀ i : ι, IsLocalization.Away (f i)
      Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i)) := fun i =>
    hV.isLocalization_basicOpen (f i)
  haveI pieceLocalized : ∀ i : ι, IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers (f i))
      (Scheme.QcohOn.secResₗ (F := D.sheaf)
        ((relCurve C B).basicOpen_le (f i)) (le_refl V)) := fun i =>
    isLocalizedModule_secResₗ_glued B D.pieces D.unit hV D.isGluingCocycle
      (fun _ _ _ => rfl) hP' i
  let e (i : ι) :
      Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i)) ⊗[Γ(relCurve C B, V)]
          (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V))
        ≃ₗ[Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i))]
          Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i)) :=
    (IsLocalizedModule.isBaseChange (Submonoid.powers (f i))
      Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i))
      (Scheme.QcohOn.secResₗ (F := D.sheaf)
        ((relCurve C B).basicOpen_le (f i)) (le_refl V))).equiv.trans

     9	/-!
    10	# The presentation locus for the rank-one Abel map
    11	
    12	`PicRankOneOpen` is the functorial locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer whose pullback to
    13	every affine test admits a tied `PicRankOneLocalPresentation`.  Quantifying after every affine
    14	pullback makes the condition intrinsic on arbitrary test schemes; stability under further
    15	pullback is exactly `picEtMap_comp`.
    16	
    17	The remaining declarations form the corresponding preimages in the widened divisor functor and
    18	in its canonical representing Yoneda functor, together with the restricted Abel transformations.
    19	These are logical subfunctors only.  In particular, this file does not assert that
    20	`PicRankOneOpen` is represented by an open subscheme.  The relative-openness acceptance gate and
    21	the conditional universal-divisor carrier contract are exposed separately in `DivRankOneOpen.lean`.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	set_option autoImplicit false
    25	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    26	
    27	universe u
    28	
    29	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    30	
    31	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    32	
    33	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    34	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    35	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    36	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    37	
    38	noncomputable section
    39	
    40	/-- The rank-one presentation locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer.
    41	
    42	Membership means that every affine pullback of the input plus class admits a local presentation
    43	tied to that pullback.  This is the correct logical subfunctor underlying the future open Picard
    44	locus; no openness or representability assertion is part of this definition. -/
    45	def PicRankOneOpen :
    46	    Subfunctor (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) where
    47	  obj T := {lam | ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    48	      (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    49	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    50	      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))}
    51	  map {T T'} f lam hlam A _ _ t := by
    52	    let F := picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)
    53	    have e : F.map t.op (F.map f lam) = F.map (t ≫ f.unop).op lam := by
    54	      apply Subtype.ext
    55	      exact (picEtMap_comp C f.unop t lam.1).symm
    56	    rw [e]
    57	    exact hlam A (t ≫ f.unop)
    58	
    59	/-! ## The public membership contract -/
    60	
    61	/-- The exact producer predicate for the rank-one locus.
    62	
    63	This is intentionally lambda-tied and quantifies over every affine pullback.  In particular, it
    64	is stronger than a field-fibre `h⁰ = 1`/`H¹ = 0` statement: a producer must supply the complete
    65	`PicRankOneLocalPresentation` structure for the pulled-back class. -/
    66	def PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition
    67	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    68	    (lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) : Prop :=
    69	  ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    70	    (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    71	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    72	      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))
    73	
    74	/-- Unfolded membership in `PicRankOneOpen`, with the presentation tied to the pulled-back
    75	Picard class.  Keeping this predicate named is important for producers in later lanes: a
    76	field-level divisor or chart witness is not a substitute for this arbitrary-affine-pullback
    77	contract. -/
    78	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_iff {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    79	    (lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) :
    80	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T ↔
    81	      ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    82	        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    83	        Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    84	          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam)) := by
    85	  rfl
    86	
    87	/-- Constructor for the exact lambda-tied arbitrary-affine-pullback presentation contract. -/
    88	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentations
    89	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    90	    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
    91	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    92	        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    93	        Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    94	          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))) :
    95	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T :=
    96	  (mem_picRankOneOpen_iff pi lam).mpr h
    97	
    98	/-- Constructor using the named arbitrary-affine producer predicate. -/
    99	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentationCondition
   100	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   101	    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   102	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition pi lam) :
   103	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T := by
   104	  exact mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentations pi h
   105	
   106	/-- The inclusion of the public rank-one locus into its degree-genus ambient functor. -/
   107	def picRankOneOpenIncl :
   108	    (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor ⟶ picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ) :=
   109	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).ι
   110	
   111	/-- The same inclusion after the slice-to-big-site `Σ` extension.
   112	
   113	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is a property of presheaves on schemes.  The rank-one functor is
   114	defined on the slice over `Spec k`, so the `Σ` extension is the category-correct carrier for the
   115	relative-open gate below. -/
   116	def picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl :
   117	    Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor ⟶
   118	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) :=
   119	  Over.sigmaExtensionNat (PicRankOneOpen pi).ι
   120	
   121	/-- Relative openness of the public locus, in Mathlib's presheaf sense.
   122	
   123	This is a named acceptance gate rather than an unproved global assertion.  A future geometric
   124	producer discharges it by supplying the represented open pullbacks; no arbitrary `Subfunctor` is
   125	silently treated as an open subscheme. -/
   126	def PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen : Prop :=
   127	  IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi)
   128	
   129	/-! ## The explicit fibre producer contract -/
   130	
   131	/-- A fibre of the rank-one locus over one test class, presented by an open of that test.
   132	
   133	The `exists_factor` field is tied to the displayed class `g` and to an arbitrary source value `v`.
   134	It is the family-level content needed for relative representability; the open immersion itself
   135	supplies uniqueness of the factor.  Thus this structure cannot be inhabited by an unrelated open
   136	or by a fieldwise dimension statement. -/
   137	structure PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented
   138	    {X : Scheme.{u}}
   139	    (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
   140	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ))) where
   141	  W : X.Opens
   142	  fst : yoneda.obj (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶
   143	    Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor
   144	  sq : fst ≫ picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi = yoneda.map W.ι ≫ g
   145	  exists_factor : ∀ (S : Scheme.{u})
   146	    (v : (Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor).obj (Opposite.op S))
   147	    (w : S ⟶ X),
   148	    (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi).app (Opposite.op S) v =
   149	      g.app (Opposite.op S) w →
   150	    ∃ u : S ⟶ (W : Scheme.{u}),
   151	      fst.app (Opposite.op S) u = v ∧ u ≫ W.ι = w
   152	
   153	namespace PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented
   154	
   155	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
   156	variable {g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
   157	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ))}
   158	
   159	/-- The fibre square supplied by `FibrePresented` is a pullback of presheaves. -/
   160	theorem isPullback (D : PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented pi g) :
   161	    IsPullback D.fst (yoneda.map D.W.ι) (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi) g := by
   162	  refine IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app fun S => ?_
   163	  rw [Types.isPullback_iff]
   164	  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
   165	  · exact congrArg (fun φ : yoneda.obj (D.W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶
   166	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) =>
   167	      φ.app S) D.sq
   168	  · rintro u₁ u₂ ⟨-, h₂⟩
   169	    exact (cancel_mono D.W.ι).mp h₂
   170	  · intro v w hvw
   171	    obtain ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩ := D.exists_factor S.unop v w hvw
   172	    exact ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩
   173	
   174	end PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented
   175	
   176	/-- An arbitrary-test fibre producer discharges the relative openness gate. -/
   177	theorem picRankOneOpen_isOpen_of_fibrePresented
   178	    (D : ∀ (X : Scheme.{u})
   179	      (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
   180	        Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ))),
   181	      PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented pi g) :
   182	    PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi := by
   183	  refine MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists ?_
   184	  intro X g
   185	  let d := D X g
   186	  exact ⟨d.W, d.fst, d.W.ι, d.isPullback, inferInstance⟩
   187	
   188	/-- Expose a supplied relative-open certificate without hiding it behind typeclass search. -/
   189	theorem picRankOneOpen_isOpen_of_certificate
   190	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi) : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi :=
   191	  h
   192	
   193	/-- Extract the open immersion supplied by the relative-openness certificate on an arbitrary
   194	pullback.  This is the exact shape consumed by an eventual chart/fibre producer. -/
   195	theorem picRankOneOpen_openPullback
   196	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi)
   197	    {X Z : Scheme.{u}}
   198	    (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
   199	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)))
   200	    (fst : yoneda.obj Z ⟶
   201	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor)
   202	    (snd : Z ⟶ X)
   203	    (hpb : IsPullback fst (yoneda.map snd) (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi) g) :
   204	    IsOpenImmersion snd :=
   205	  h.property g fst snd hpb
   206	
   207	/-- Pullback stability of the public rank-one locus, exposed independently of its definition. -/
   208	theorem picRankOneOpen_map_mem {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   209	    (f : T ⟶ T') {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   210	    (h : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T) :
   211	    (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map f lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T' :=
   212	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).map f h
   213	
   214	/-- Pullback stability of the public locus, with the base-change direction made explicit. -/
   215	theorem picRankOneOpen_baseChange_mem {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   216	    (f : T ⟶ T') {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   217	    (h : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T) :
   218	    (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map f lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T' :=
   219	  picRankOneOpen_map_mem pi f h
   220	
   221	/-- The inverse image of `PicRankOneOpen` under the affine widened Abel transformation.
   222	
   223	This name deliberately records only a presentation-theoretic preimage.  It is not the future
   224	open subscheme `DivRankOneOpen`. -/
   225	def divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff :
   226	    Subfunctor (divFunctorAff C (genus C)) :=
   227	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).preimage (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C))
   228	
   229	/-- The same presentation preimage on the Yoneda functor of the canonical genus divisor
   230	representer. -/
   231	def divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter :
   232	    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)) :=
   233	  (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).preimage
   234	    (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom
   235	
   236	/-- The affine Abel transformation restricted to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
   237	def rankOneAbelAff :
   238	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).toFunctor ⟶
   239	      (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor :=
   240	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).fromPreimage (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C))
   241	
   242	/-- Restrict the canonical representation isomorphism to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
   243	def rankOneRepresenterRestriction :
   244	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor ⟶
   245	      (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).toFunctor :=
   246	  (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).fromPreimage
   247	    (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom
   248	
   249	/-- The represented genus Abel map restricted to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
   250	def rankOneAbelRepresented :
   251	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor ⟶
   252	      (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor :=
   253	  rankOneRepresenterRestriction pi ≫ rankOneAbelAff pi

   257	theorem records the exact target API that consumer lanes can use today. -/
   258	theorem rankOneAbelRepresented_mem {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   259	    (x : (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).obj T) :

   261	      (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T :=
   262	  ((rankOneAbelRepresented pi).app T x).property

    11

    39	/-- The universal genus-divisor predicate whose Abel class lies in `PicRankOneOpen`. -/

    44	/-- Evaluation of the represented genus Abel map on a slice point, with the base morphism

    56	      (Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k))
    57	        (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ))).obj (op T.left)) =

    74	    (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C)).app
    75	      (op (Over.mk (q.left ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom)))
    76	      ((divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv q')
    77	  have hnat := ConcreteCategory.congr_hom
    78	    ((abelDivAffTrans C (genus C)).naturality e.op)
    79	      ((divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv q)
    80	  have hhom :
    81	      (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv q' =
    82	        (divFunctorAff C (genus C)).map e.op
    83	          ((divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv q) := by
    84	    calc
    85	      (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv q' =
    86	          (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv (e ≫ q) := by
    87	            rw [hq]
    88	      _ = (divFunctorAff C (genus C)).map e.op
    89	          ((divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv q) :=
    90	        (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv_comp e q
    91	  rw [hhom]
    92	  simpa only [ConcreteCategory.comp_apply] using hnat.symm
    93	
    94	/-- A represented genus divisor lies in the universal predicate exactly when its Abel image
    95	lifts through the single public rank-one Picard locus. -/
    96	theorem divRankOneUniversalPredicate_mem_iff_sigma
    97	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    98	    (x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T) :
    99	    x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T ↔
   100	      ∃ v : (Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k))
   101	          (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor).obj (op T.unop.left),
   102	        (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi).app (op T.unop.left) v =
   103	          (abelDivAffGenusSigma C).app (op T.unop.left) x.left := by
   104	  simp only [divRankOneUniversalPredicate,
   105	    divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter,
   106	    Subfunctor.preimage_obj, Set.mem_preimage]
   107	  let p := (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C)).app T
   108	    ((divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv x)
   109	  change p ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T ↔ _
   110	  have hleft :
   111	      (abelDivAffGenusSigma C).app (op T.unop.left) x.left =
   112	        (⟨T.unop.hom, p⟩ :
   113	          (Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k))
   114	            (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ))).obj
   115	              (op T.unop.left)) :=
   116	    abelDivAffGenusSigma_app_left_rankOne x
   117	  constructor
   118	  · intro hp
   119	    refine ⟨⟨T.unop.hom, ⟨p, hp⟩⟩, ?_⟩
   120	    rw [hleft]
   121	    rfl
   122	  · rintro ⟨v, hv⟩
   123	    rw [hleft] at hv
   124	    dsimp [picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl,
   125	      CategoryTheory.Over.sigmaExtensionNat] at hv
   126	    rcases v with ⟨a, y⟩
   127	    dsimp at hv
   128	    have hfirst : a = T.unop.hom :=
   129	      congrArg (fun z => z.1) hv
   130	    cases hfirst
   131	    have hinj := Sigma.mk.inj hv
   132	    have heq :
   133	        ConcreteCategory.hom
   134	            ((PicRankOneOpen pi).ι.app
   135	              (op (Over.mk T.unop.hom))) y = p :=
   136	      eq_of_heq hinj.2
   137	    change p ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T
   138	    rw [← heq]
   139	    exact y.property
   140	
   141	/-- The Yoneda map induced by the inclusion of an open of an object in the slice.  Naming this
   142	map is useful to consumers which need the actual factorisation through the open, rather than only
   143	the proposition that a point lies in its range. -/
   144	def openSubfunctorMap (D : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : D.left.Opens) :
   145	    yoneda.obj (Over.mk (U.ι ≫ D.hom)) ⟶ yoneda.obj D :=
   146	  yoneda.map (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk (U.ι ≫ D.hom)) U.ι)
   147	
   148	/-- The subfunctor represented by an open `U` of an object `D` in the slice over `Spec k`.
   149	
   150	Its values are precisely morphisms which factor through the open immersion `U.ι`; using the
   151	Yoneda range keeps this definition independent of any chosen affine presentation of `U`. -/
   152	def openSubfunctor (D : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : D.left.Opens) :
   153	    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj D) :=
   154	  Subfunctor.range (openSubfunctorMap D U)
   155	
   156	/-- Unpack range membership into the actual source point and its equality in the ambient Yoneda
   157	functor.  This is the pointwise factorisation API used by inverse constructions. -/
   158	theorem openSubfunctor_mem_iff
   159	    (D : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : D.left.Opens)
   160	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   161	    (x : (yoneda.obj D).obj T) :
   162	    x ∈ (openSubfunctor D U).obj T ↔
   163	      ∃ y : (yoneda.obj (Over.mk (U.ι ≫ D.hom))).obj T,
   164	        (openSubfunctorMap D U).app T y = x := by
   165	  rfl
   166	
   167	/-- An explicit geometric certificate for the universal rank-one predicate.
   168	
   169	The equality is the missing family-level producer/gluing statement: it identifies the logical
   170	preimage with an actual open of the canonical genus representer.  No default or top-open witness
   171	is manufactured here. -/
   172	structure DivRankOneOpenData (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi] where
   173	  carrier : (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left.Opens
   174	  carrier_eq :
   175	    openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) carrier =
   176	      divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi
   177	
   178	/-- Genuine relative openness of the public Picard rank-one locus produces the universal
   179	divisor rank-one open.  The carrier is the open image of the represented pullback of the Abel
   180	map, and the proof below identifies its Yoneda range with the defining predicate. -/
   181	theorem divRankOneOpenData_of_picRankOneOpen_isOpen
   182	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi) :
   183	    Nonempty (DivRankOneOpenData pi) := by
   184	  obtain ⟨X, snd, fst, hpb⟩ := h.rep (abelDivAffGenusSigma C)
   185	  letI : IsOpenImmersion snd :=
   186	    h.property (abelDivAffGenusSigma C) fst snd hpb
   187	  let U := snd.opensRange
   188	  refine ⟨⟨U, ?_⟩⟩
   189	  ext T x
   190	  rw [openSubfunctor_mem_iff]
   191	  rw [divRankOneUniversalPredicate_mem_iff_sigma]
   192	  have hpbT := (IsPullback.iff_app.mp hpb) (op T.unop.left)
   193	  rw [Types.isPullback_iff] at hpbT
   194	  constructor
   195	  · rintro ⟨y, hy⟩
   196	    have hxy : x.left = y.left ≫ U.ι := by
   197	      have hleft := congrArg Over.Hom.left hy
   198	      exact hleft.symm
   199	    have hrange : Set.range x.left.base ⊆ Set.range snd.base := by
   200	      rw [← Scheme.Hom.coe_opensRange snd]
   201	      rintro z ⟨t, rfl⟩
   202	      rw [hxy, Scheme.Hom.comp_apply]
   203	      change U.ι.base (y.left.base t) ∈ snd.opensRange
   204	      change U.ι.base (y.left.base t) ∈ U
   205	      exact (y.left.base t).property
   206	    let u : T.unop.left ⟶ X :=
   207	      IsOpenImmersion.lift snd x.left hrange
   208	    have hu : u ≫ snd = x.left :=
   209	      IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac _ _ _
   210	    refine ⟨fst.app (op T.unop.left) u, ?_⟩
   211	    have hcomm := congrArg
   212	      (fun f => (ConcreteCategory.hom f) u) hpbT.1
   213	    change (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi).app (op T.unop.left)
   214	        (fst.app (op T.unop.left) u) =
   215	      (abelDivAffGenusSigma C).app (op T.unop.left) (u ≫ snd) at hcomm
   216	    simpa only [hu] using hcomm
   217	  · rintro ⟨v, hv⟩
   218	    obtain ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩ := hpbT.2.2 v x.left hv
   219	    change u ≫ snd = x.left at hu₂
   220	    have hrange : Set.range x.left.base ⊆ Set.range U.ι.base := by
   221	      rw [Scheme.Opens.range_ι]
   222	      change Set.range x.left.base ⊆ snd.opensRange
   223	      rw [Scheme.Hom.coe_opensRange]
   224	      rintro z ⟨t, rfl⟩
   225	      refine ⟨u.base t, ?_⟩
   226	      have happ := congrArg (fun f => f.base t) hu₂
   227	      simpa only [Scheme.Hom.comp_apply] using happ
   228	    let V : Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
   229	      Over.mk (U.ι ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom)
   230	    let j : V ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C :=
   231	      Over.homMk (U := V) U.ι
   232	    let e : U.toScheme = V.left := rfl
   233	    let l : T.unop.left ⟶ U.toScheme :=
   234	      IsOpenImmersion.lift U.ι x.left hrange
   235	    let l' : T.unop.left ⟶ V.left := l ≫ eqToHom e
   236	    have he : eqToHom e ≫ j.left = U.ι := by
   237	      subst e
   238	      rfl
   239	    have hl : l' ≫ j.left = x.left := by
   240	      dsimp only [l']
   241	      rw [Category.assoc, he]
   242	      dsimp only [l]
   243	      exact IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac _ _ _
   244	    have hlw : l' ≫ V.hom = T.unop.hom := by
   245	      rw [← j.w, ← Category.assoc, hl]
   246	      exact x.w
   247	    let y : (yoneda.obj V).obj T := Over.homMk l' hlw
   248	    refine ⟨y, ?_⟩
   249	    change y ≫ j = x
   250	    apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
   251	    exact hl
   252	
   253	/-- A named carrier choice for consumers which already possess the Picard openness theorem. -/
   254	def divRankOneOpenDataOfPicRankOneOpen
   255	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi) : DivRankOneOpenData pi :=
   256	  Classical.choice (divRankOneOpenData_of_picRankOneOpen_isOpen pi h)
   257	
   258	/-- The open subscheme supplied by a `DivRankOneOpenData` witness. -/
   259	def DivRankOneOpen (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) : Scheme :=
   260	  h.carrier.toScheme
   261	
   262	/-- The canonical open immersion into the genus divisor representer. -/
   263	def divRankOneOpenMap (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
   264	    DivRankOneOpen pi h ⟶ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left :=
   265	  h.carrier.ι
   266	
   267	theorem divRankOneOpen_isOpenImmersion
   268	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
   269	    IsOpenImmersion (divRankOneOpenMap pi h) := by
   270	  change IsOpenImmersion h.carrier.ι
   271	  infer_instance
   272	
   273	/- The scheme-level certificate also has the presheaf form consumed by relative-open inverse
   274	   constructions.  This is conditional only on the explicit carrier witness above. -/
   275	theorem divRankOneOpenMap_presheaf_isOpenImmersion
   276	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
   277	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (yoneda.map (divRankOneOpenMap pi h)) := by
   278	  exact MorphismProperty.relative_map (divRankOneOpen_isOpenImmersion pi h)
   279	
   280	/-- The open represented object, retained in the slice over `Spec k` for consumers of the affine
   281	divisor functor. -/
   282	def divRankOneOpenOver (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
   283	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
   284	  Over.mk (divRankOneOpenMap pi h ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom)
   285	
   286	/-- The inclusion of the certified open, as a morphism in the slice over `Spec k`.
   287	
   288	This is the map whose Yoneda action is consumed by the canonical rank-one Abel inverse.  Naming
   289	it separately keeps consumers independent of the implementation spelling of `divRankOneOpenOver`.
   290	-/
   291	def divRankOneOpenOverMap (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
   292	    divRankOneOpenOver pi h ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C :=
   293	  Over.homMk (divRankOneOpenMap pi h)
   294	
   295	/-- Pull back the certified rank-one open along an arbitrary slice morphism. -/
   296	def divRankOneOpenPullback
   297	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   298	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C) : T.left.Opens :=
   299	  q.left ⁻¹ᵁ h.carrier
   300	
   301	theorem divRankOneOpenPullback_isOpenImmersion
   302	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   303	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C) :
   304	    IsOpenImmersion (divRankOneOpenPullback pi h q).ι := by
   305	  infer_instance
   306	
   307	/-- The arbitrary slice pullback remains an open immersion after passing to Yoneda. -/
   308	theorem divRankOneOpenPullbackMap_presheaf_isOpenImmersion
   309	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   310	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C) :
   311	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf
   312	      (yoneda.map (divRankOneOpenPullback pi h q).ι) := by
   313	  exact MorphismProperty.relative_map (divRankOneOpenPullback_isOpenImmersion pi h q)
   314	
   315	/-- Pointwise form of arbitrary base-change compatibility for the certified open. -/
   316	theorem mem_divRankOneOpenPullback_iff
   317	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   318	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C)
   319	    (x : T.left) :
   320	    x ∈ divRankOneOpenPullback pi h q ↔ q.left.base x ∈ h.carrier := by
   321	  rfl
   322	
   323	/-- The universal predicate is exactly the represented preimage used by the Abel restriction. -/
   324	theorem divRankOneUniversalPredicate_eq_preimage :
   325	    divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi = divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi :=
   326	  rfl
   327	
   328	/-- The certified open carrier has the universal rank-one predicate as its Yoneda range. -/
   329	theorem divRankOneOpen_carrier_eq
   330	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
   331	    openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier =
   332	      divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi :=
   333	  h.carrier_eq
   334	
   335	/-- Pointwise form of the witness equality, exposing the exact contract consumed by an inverse.
   336	
   337	The right-hand side is the range of the open immersion, so a consumer can use this theorem to
   338	replace a rank-one predicate proof by a factorisation through `DivRankOneOpen pi h`. -/
   339	theorem divRankOneOpen_mem_iff
   340	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   341	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   342	    (x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T) :
   343	    x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T ↔
   344	      x ∈ (openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier).obj T := by
   345	  rw [h.carrier_eq]
   346	
   347	/-- A point of the universal rank-one predicate factors through the certified open immersion.
   348	
   349	Unlike a bare range-membership proof, the conclusion exposes the source point and the equality
   350	of its image with the given divisor point, which is the exact data needed by a canonical inverse. -/
   351	theorem divRankOneOpen_mem_iff_factorization
   352	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   353	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   354	    (x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T) :
   355	    x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T ↔
   356	      ∃ y : (yoneda.obj (Over.mk
   357	          (h.carrier.ι ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom))).obj T,
   358	        (openSubfunctorMap (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier).app T y = x := by
   359	  rw [divRankOneOpen_mem_iff pi h x, openSubfunctor_mem_iff]
   360	
   361	/-- The same factorisation contract with the named open object and slice inclusion.
   362	
   363	The source in the preceding theorem is definitionally the slice object
   364	`divRankOneOpenOver pi h`; this corollary gives the stable public names expected by inverse
   365	consumers. -/
   366	theorem divRankOneOpen_mem_iff_factorization_over
   367	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   368	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   369	    (x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T) :
   370	    x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T ↔
   371	      ∃ y : (yoneda.obj (divRankOneOpenOver pi h)).obj T,
   372	        (yoneda.map (divRankOneOpenOverMap pi h)).app T y = x := by
   373	  rw [divRankOneOpen_mem_iff_factorization pi h x]
   374	  rfl
   375	
   376	/-- The exact inverse-facing factorisation for a point of the represented rank-one preimage.
   377	
   378	The source point is retained as a subtype, so its membership proof is tied to the same divisor
   379	that is factored through `DivRankOneOpenOver`; no unrelated class or top-open witness can satisfy
   380	this endpoint. -/
   381	theorem rankOneRepresenterRestriction_factorization
   382	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   383	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   384	    (x : (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).obj T) :
   385	    ∃ y : (yoneda.obj (divRankOneOpenOver pi h)).obj T,
   386	      (yoneda.map (divRankOneOpenOverMap pi h)).app T y = x.1 := by
   387	  apply (divRankOneOpen_mem_iff_factorization_over pi h x.1).mp
   388	  exact x.2
   389	
   390	/-- Immediate inverse-facing consumer of Picard rank-one openness: every point of the represented
   391	rank-one divisor preimage factors through the open carrier extracted from that certificate. -/
   392	theorem rankOneRepresenterRestriction_factorization_of_picRankOneOpen_isOpen
   393	    (hPic : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi)
   394	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   395	    (x : (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).obj T) :
   396	    ∃ y : (yoneda.obj (divRankOneOpenOver pi
   397	        (divRankOneOpenDataOfPicRankOneOpen pi hPic))).obj T,
   398	      (yoneda.map (divRankOneOpenOverMap pi
   399	        (divRankOneOpenDataOfPicRankOneOpen pi hPic))).app T y = x.1 :=
   400	  rankOneRepresenterRestriction_factorization pi
   401	    (divRankOneOpenDataOfPicRankOneOpen pi hPic) x
   402	
   403	/-- A point in the certified open carrier is a point of the universal rank-one predicate. -/
   404	theorem divRankOneOpen_mem_of_carrier
   405	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   406	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   407	    {x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T}
   408	    (hx : x ∈ (openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier).obj T) :
   409	    x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T := by
   410	  exact (divRankOneOpen_mem_iff pi h x).mpr hx
   411	
   412	/- The logical rank-one predicate remains stable under arbitrary pullback, independently of the
   413	   geometric witness used to represent it by an open. -/
   414	theorem divRankOneOpen_baseChange_mem
   415	    {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   416	    (f : T ⟶ T')
   417	    {x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T}
   418	    (hx : x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T) :
   419	    (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).map f x ∈
   420	      (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T' :=
   421	  (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).map f hx
   422	
   423	end
   424	
   425	end AlgebraicGeometry

data.content:
1	/-

     5	-/
     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.ModulesBaseSheaf
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.ModulesPushforwardBaseChange
     8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafH0BaseChange
     9	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.LocalGenerators
    10	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AdmissibleAbelEtaleSurjectiveH0BaseChange
    11	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AdmissibleAbelEtaleSurjectiveSite
    12	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0EndgameContract
    13	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RingDatumEngine
    14	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SectionsToDivisorsClass
    15	
    16	/-!
    17	# The local-presentation contract for the rank-one Picard locus
    18	
    19	An element of `picDegLayerFunctor` is an etale-plus class, not a chosen line bundle.  The
    20	rank-one route therefore needs an explicit local presentation before it can use the evaluation
    21	map of a line bundle.  `PicRankOneLocalPresentation` records that presentation on an affine
    22	test and ties every piece of data to the input class:
    23	
    24	* a descent-class representative whose plus class is the affine collapse of the input;
    25	* a cocycle datum presenting that same relative Picard class;
    26	* a locally free rank-one `Scheme.Modules` object whose base-ring sheaf is the datum's sheaf;
    27	* invertibility of the canonical native pushforward base-change mate on every cartesian square;
    28	* the cohomological rank-one outputs used by the evaluation construction.
    29	
    30	No existence, openness, or representability assertion is made here.  The first canonical
    31	consumer is `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.evaluation`, the pullback-pushforward counit.
    32	The method `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.h0BaseChange` derives arbitrary affine base change
    33	from the same presentation's `H^1`-vanishing field.  The section bridge at the end identifies
    34	datum `H^0` with native global sections and proves, by the adjunction triangle identity, that
    35	the evaluation counit sends the canonical unit-lift back to that same section.
    36	-/
    37	
    38	set_option autoImplicit false
    39	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    40	
    41	universe u
    42	
    43	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
    44	  CartesianMonoidalCategory
    45	
    46	open scoped TensorProduct
    47	
    48	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    49	
    50	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    51	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    52	
    53	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    54	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    55	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    56	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    57	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    58	
    59	/-- A rank-one presentation of a genus-degree plus class on an affine test.
    60	
    61	The two equality fields prevent an unrelated cocycle datum or line bundle from serving as a
    62	witness: `representative` presents the input plus class, `datum_class` presents that same
    63	relative Picard class, and `module_iso` identifies the resulting cocycle sheaf with the
    64	underlying base-ring sheaf of `module`. -/
    65	structure PicRankOneLocalPresentation
    66	    (lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)) : Type (u + 1) where
